fields.apa_citation: Jennings, P., & Cain, R. (2012). A framework for improving urban soundscapes. Applied Acoustics. Advance online publication (available online 15 January 2012). [Volume, issue, and page numbers are not printed in the extracted docling text.]
fields.main_conclusion: The authors propose a three-part conceptual framework — describing a soundscape's objective composition, the (mostly non-acoustic) factors that make it feel positive, and, via an adapted Kano model, how design interventions map onto basic/performance/excitement levels of listener engagement — arguing that whether an urban soundscape feels positive depends chiefly on what activity the user is doing rather than on sound level alone.
fields.construct_pair: Urban-space design interventions (soundscape composition and context) -> perceived positivity of the space
fields.methods_surface_summary: Conceptual/framework paper with no original data collection: it synthesizes prior soundscape-perception literature and adapts the Kano model (from product-development/automotive sound-quality research) into a three-part planning framework, illustrated with references to a companion listening study (not itself reported here) on the emotional dimensions of 'calmness' and 'vibrancy'.

notes.apa_citation: Authors, title, journal, and an 'Available online 15 January 2012' date are printed in the docling text, giving reasonable confidence in a 2012 year, but no volume/issue/page range appears anywhere in the extracted file, so the citation is left incomplete rather than fabricated.
notes.article_type: This is a position/framework paper (no participants, no original measurements), so it is coded theoretical rather than any empirical category; it is closer to a 'commentary/framework' piece but does propose a structured conceptual model with sections, so 'theoretical' was judged the best fit of the offered categories.
notes.sample_n / p_value / effect_size / stimu: All null because the paper reports no original empirical study — it references a separate companion paper (Cain, Jennings & Poxon, cited in the reference list) that contains the actual listening-test data, but that study's numbers are not reproduced in this text.
notes.direction: 'not_applicable' because there is no IV->DV empirical test in this document.
